---
name: all-or-none-rule-commitment-fails
description: Committing to the single smallest consistent rule (no posterior averaging) fits ~170 nats worse than the best Bayesian model
metadata:
  type: project
---
Round 1 candidate 2 (2026-10-30), `smallest_rule_commitment`: commit to the smallest consistent rule out of 44 arithmetic+digit rules (span fallback), plus 2 yes-rates. Smoke-fit log-lik was about -1088, against an ELPD of -918 for `tenenbaum_digit_concepts`. Only 200 of 2250 trials needed the fallback.

**Why:** people's generalization is graded, so averaging over hypotheses (and intervals) matters. Hard MAP commitment is too coarse.
**How to apply:** don't bother with more variants of deterministic MAP/rule commitment. Graded posterior mixing is needed. See [[digit-concepts-key]].
---
name: digit-concepts-key
description: In the number-game data, "contains digit d" concepts drive much of the fit; Tenenbaum+digit rules hits ~-914 in-sample loglik with 2 params
metadata:
  type: project
---
Raw responses show digit-containment generalization (set 83,38,58,68 → yes to 84-89; 92,82,27,42 → yes to 20s), and distance-to-nearest-example barely matters. Adding 11 digit concepts (contains 0-9, ends in 0) to tenenbaum_rules_similarity (round 0, candidate_5, `tenenbaum_digit_concepts`) gave smoke-fit loglik -914.4, vs incumbent bigelow_piantadosi_independent ELPD-LOO -926.6 (45 free rule weights).

**Why:** the digit rules were the gap between Tenenbaum (-1249) and the incumbent, not the per-rule weights.
**How to apply:** future refinements should keep the digit concepts; free per-rule weights may be unnecessary.

Round 1 cand_1: `conservative_evidence_digit_concepts` (likelihood tempered by power beta, LogNormal(0,0.5)) smoke-fit loglik -913.8 — only ~0.6 better than the untempered model, so evidence tempering probably isn't where the gap is.

Round 1 (candidate_3) MAP tests on the incumbent: a free prior share for digit concepts fits omega≈0.255 (= the equal-weight 11/44, so no gain, novelty risk); freeing NOISE gives noise≈0.136, LL -910.8; a guess lapse gives lapse≈0.028, LL -909.0. Submitted the free-noise version (`digit_concepts_inferred_outlier_rate`).
---
name: fit-speed-budget
description: Admission fit is 7000 iters/chain warm-start NUTS; per-gradient cost must be ~<25ms; tricks that worked
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 1d82c78b-0bac-4618-97c8-da7bd32baa1b
  modified: 2026-10-30T21:06:41.047Z
---

Admission fits use production draws 4000 + tune 3000 per chain (warm_start_nuts, dense mass matrix), 30-min limit per run. Machine has 1 core. Incumbent `tenenbaum_digit_concepts` logp+grad ≈ 12 ms. A memory-subset mixture over its hypothesis space (≈700 states) cost 62 ms naive → too slow (~49 min).

**Why:** the check_candidate smoke fit (200 iters) passes even when the full fit would time out.

**How to apply:** benchmark logp+dlogp time and NUTS n_steps (probe `_warm_start_sample` with small draws) before finishing. Speedups that worked: replace gathering posterior rows per cell (slow AdvancedIncSubtensor1 gradient) with a `pytensor.sparse.CSR` + `structured_dot` (44→25 ms); declaring module-level `SAMPLER_SETTINGS = {"target_accept": 0.9}` halves steps (10.8→5.3). Don't name a scratch script `timeit.py` (shadows stdlib, breaks pymc import). Related: [[digit-concepts-key]].

Also worked (2026-10-30, `order_weighted_concept_learning`): when intervals must be grouped by (size, per-position hit pattern) instead of (size, k), keep only each set's non-empty groups (≤473 of 1600 on this data) padded per set, and gather size-dependent terms by index — 47 → 18 ms.
---
name: lapse-small-gain
description: Adding guess-lapse or free noise to tenenbaum_digit_concepts gains only ~2-4 nats smoke loglik; a hand-rolled find_MAP loglik script gave bogus numbers
metadata:
  type: project
---
Round 1 candidate_4 (2026-10-30): `digit_concepts_with_guess_lapse` (incumbent + eps/g lapse) smoke loglik -910.4; free NOISE ~Beta(2,8) variant -912.2; incumbent ~-914.4 ([[digit-concepts-key]]).

**Why:** my own MAP script, built with pm.logp + compile_fn, reported -1264 for the base model, which is wrong. Trust check_candidate's smoke loglik instead.
**How to apply:** small response-level tweaks are close to saturated; bigger gains probably need hypothesis-space changes.
- [Digit concepts are key](digit-concepts-key.md) — contains-digit rules explain most of the fit gap
- [All-or-none rule commitment fails](all-or-none-rule-commitment-fails.md) — MAP smallest-rule learner ~170 nats behind
- [Number-game ceiling](number-game-ceiling.md) — one-parameter tweaks only gain 3-6 nats; residual sets listed
- [Lapse small gain](lapse-small-gain.md) — lapse/noise tweaks on digit model gain only ~2-4 nats; don't trust ad-hoc MAP loglik
- [Fit speed budget](fit-speed-budget.md) — admission is 7000 iters/chain; benchmark grad time; sparse CSR + target_accept 0.9 tricks
---
name: number-game-ceiling
description: Rule+interval+digit concept model is near its ceiling; single-param tweaks gain only 3-6 nats in-sample
metadata:
  type: project
---
Round 1 (iter_1, candidate_5) MAP screens with equal-weight 44-rule + uniform-interval model (in-sample NLL 912): free example-noise 908.5, lapse 907.9, noise+lapse 906.3, logit response map 908.6, size-principle exponent 911.6, Erlang interval prior 913.5 (uniform is better), rule-family weights about 911, free 45 weights 893 (but the extra params cost it on LOO). Calibration by predicted-p bin is already good. Biggest per-set residuals: 83,38,58,68 (scattered 20-40% yes in the 50s-70s), 85,19,91 (odd numbers overpredicted), 14,47.
Submitted `equal_prior_concepts_with_guess_lapse` (the lapse model with one shared rule prior): smoke loglik -905.8.

**Why:** the next improvement probably needs a new mechanism, not another response or prior parameter. Builds on [[digit-concepts-key]].
**How to apply:** don't spend rounds on noise/lapse/exponent tweaks; look at the residual sets above.

"""Refinement of concept_learning_with_guess_lapse: Bayesian concept learning
over the same 45 rules and every interval of 1..100 (size principle, 10% of
examples drawn uniformly), plus a response lapse -- on a fraction `lapse` of
trials the participant ignores the concept and answers "yes" with probability
`guess_yes`. The one change: no learned preference among rules. All 45 rules
share the rule prior lambda_0 equally, instead of 45 separately inferred
weights; each interval keeps prior (1 - lambda_0) / 5050.
"""

import numpy as np
import pymc as pm
import pytensor.tensor as pt
from scipy.special import logsumexp

ALPHA = 0.9
NUMBERS = np.arange(1, 101)


def rule_concepts():
    rules = {
        "odd": [n for n in NUMBERS if n % 2 == 1],
        "primes": [n for n in NUMBERS if n > 1 and all(n % a for a in range(2, int(n**0.5) + 1))],
        "squares": [n * n for n in range(1, 11)],
        "cubes": [n**3 for n in range(1, 5)],
        "powers of 2, not 32": [2, 4, 8, 16, 64],
        "powers of 2, or 37": [2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 37, 64],
        "even": list(range(2, 101, 2)),
    }
    rules.update({f"multiples of {m}": list(range(m, 101, m)) for m in [3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 11, 12]})
    rules.update({f"powers of {m}": [m**k for k in range(1, 8) if m**k <= 100] for m in range(2, 11)})
    rules.update({f"ends in {d}": [n for n in NUMBERS if n % 10 == d] for d in range(10)})
    rules.update({f"contains digit {d}": [n for n in NUMBERS if str(d) in str(n)] for d in range(10)})
    return list(rules.values())


RULES = rule_concepts()
N_RULES = len(RULES)
INTERVALS = [list(range(m, n + 1)) for m in NUMBERS for n in range(m, 101)]
MEMBERSHIP = np.array([np.isin(NUMBERS, c) for c in RULES + INTERVALS], dtype="float64")
# log P(x | h) of one example x (column x - 1) under each hypothesis.
EXAMPLE_LOG_LIK = np.log(ALPHA * MEMBERSHIP / MEMBERSHIP.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True) + (1 - ALPHA) / 100)
RULE_MEMBERSHIP = MEMBERSHIP[:N_RULES]

# With equal priors the rules' and intervals' likelihoods are parameter-free,
# so prepare_observed collapses each class per example set: total evidence
# and, per target, the evidence-weighted share of hypotheses containing it.
# The posterior is then a two-way split between "a rule" and "an interval".

with pm.Model() as model:
    rule_log_evidence = pm.Data("rule_log_evidence", np.zeros(1))  # (sets,): log sum_r P(D | r)
    rule_in_concept = pm.Data("rule_in_concept", np.zeros((1, 100)))  # (sets, targets)
    interval_log_evidence = pm.Data("interval_log_evidence", np.zeros(1))  # (sets,)
    interval_in_concept = pm.Data("interval_in_concept", np.zeros((1, 100)))  # (sets, targets)
    row_cell = pm.Data("row_cell", np.zeros(1, dtype="int64"))  # set index * 100 + target - 1
    rating = pm.Data("rating", np.zeros(1, dtype="int64"))

    lambda_0 = pm.Beta("lambda_0", 2, 2)
    log_rules = pt.log(lambda_0) - np.log(N_RULES) + rule_log_evidence
    log_intervals = pt.log1p(-lambda_0) - np.log(len(INTERVALS)) + interval_log_evidence
    p_rule = pm.math.sigmoid(log_rules - log_intervals)[:, None]  # posterior that the concept is a rule
    in_concept = p_rule * rule_in_concept + (1 - p_rule) * interval_in_concept

    # Rounding can put a sure membership a few ulps above 1.
    p_concept = pt.clip(in_concept.reshape((-1,))[row_cell], 0.0, 1.0)
    lapse = pm.Beta("lapse", 2, 8)  # share of trials answered by guessing
    guess_yes = pm.Beta("guess_yes", 2, 2)  # P(yes) when guessing
    p_yes = pm.Deterministic("p_yes", pt.clip((1 - lapse) * p_concept + lapse * guess_yes, 1e-6, 1 - 1e-6))
    pm.Bernoulli("response", p=p_yes, observed=rating)


def prepare_observed(rows):
    """Rows carry `number_set` ("16,8", in presented order), `target` and `rating`."""
    sets = [tuple(int(x) for x in str(r["number_set"]).split(",")) for r in rows]
    unique = list(dict.fromkeys(sets))
    index = {s: i for i, s in enumerate(unique)}
    set_log_lik = np.stack([EXAMPLE_LOG_LIK[:, np.array(s) - 1].sum(axis=1) for s in unique])
    out = {}
    for name, part in [("rule", slice(0, N_RULES)), ("interval", slice(N_RULES, None))]:
        log_lik = set_log_lik[:, part]
        log_evidence = logsumexp(log_lik, axis=1)
        out[f"{name}_log_evidence"] = log_evidence
        out[f"{name}_in_concept"] = np.exp(log_lik - log_evidence[:, None]) @ MEMBERSHIP[part]
    out["row_cell"] = np.array([index[s] * 100 + int(r["target"]) - 1 for s, r in zip(sets, rows)], dtype="int64")
    out["rating"] = np.array([int(r["rating"]) for r in rows], dtype="int64")
    return out

"""Bayesian concept learning over equal-prior rules (arithmetic and digit
concepts) and every interval of 1..100 (size principle, 10% of examples drawn
uniformly), with a decision rule at a confidence criterion: the participant
says "yes" when the log-odds that the concept contains the target exceed the
log-odds of a personal criterion, with a fitted sensitivity (gain) to that gap
-- rather than probability matching the posterior.
"""

import numpy as np
import pymc as pm
import pytensor.tensor as pt
from scipy.special import logsumexp

ALPHA = 0.9
NUMBERS = np.arange(1, 101)


def rule_concepts():
    rules = {
        "odd": [n for n in NUMBERS if n % 2 == 1],
        "primes": [n for n in NUMBERS if n > 1 and all(n % a for a in range(2, int(n**0.5) + 1))],
        "squares": [n * n for n in range(1, 11)],
        "cubes": [n**3 for n in range(1, 5)],
        "powers of 2, not 32": [2, 4, 8, 16, 64],
        "powers of 2, or 37": [2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 37, 64],
        "even": list(range(2, 101, 2)),
    }
    rules.update({f"multiples of {m}": list(range(m, 101, m)) for m in [3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 11, 12]})
    rules.update({f"powers of {m}": [m**k for k in range(1, 8) if m**k <= 100] for m in range(2, 11)})
    rules.update({f"ends in {d}": [n for n in NUMBERS if n % 10 == d] for d in range(10)})
    rules.update({f"contains digit {d}": [n for n in NUMBERS if str(d) in str(n)] for d in range(10)})
    return list(rules.values())


RULES = rule_concepts()
N_RULES = len(RULES)
INTERVALS = [list(range(m, n + 1)) for m in NUMBERS for n in range(m, 101)]
MEMBERSHIP = np.array([np.isin(NUMBERS, c) for c in RULES + INTERVALS], dtype="float64")
# log P(x | h) of one example x (column x - 1) under each hypothesis.
EXAMPLE_LOG_LIK = np.log(ALPHA * MEMBERSHIP / MEMBERSHIP.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True) + (1 - ALPHA) / 100)

# With equal priors within each class, prepare_observed collapses rules and
# intervals per example set into total evidence and per-target membership.

with pm.Model() as model:
    rule_log_evidence = pm.Data("rule_log_evidence", np.zeros(1))  # (sets,)
    rule_in_concept = pm.Data("rule_in_concept", np.zeros((1, 100)))  # (sets, targets)
    interval_log_evidence = pm.Data("interval_log_evidence", np.zeros(1))  # (sets,)
    interval_in_concept = pm.Data("interval_in_concept", np.zeros((1, 100)))  # (sets, targets)
    row_cell = pm.Data("row_cell", np.zeros(1, dtype="int64"))  # set index * 100 + target - 1
    rating = pm.Data("rating", np.zeros(1, dtype="int64"))

    lambda_0 = pm.Beta("lambda_0", 2, 2)
    log_rules = pt.log(lambda_0) - np.log(N_RULES) + rule_log_evidence
    log_intervals = pt.log1p(-lambda_0) - np.log(len(INTERVALS)) + interval_log_evidence
    p_rule = pm.math.sigmoid(log_rules - log_intervals)[:, None]
    in_concept = p_rule * rule_in_concept + (1 - p_rule) * interval_in_concept
    p_concept = pt.clip(in_concept.reshape((-1,))[row_cell], 1e-6, 1 - 1e-6)

    # Decision rule: graded threshold on confidence.
    criterion = pm.Beta("criterion", 2, 2)  # how sure one must be to say yes
    gain = pm.LogNormal("gain", mu=0.0, sigma=0.5)  # sensitivity to confidence minus criterion
    gap = pt.log(p_concept) - pt.log1p(-p_concept) - (pt.log(criterion) - pt.log1p(-criterion))
    p_yes = pm.Deterministic("p_yes", pt.clip(pm.math.sigmoid(gain * gap), 1e-6, 1 - 1e-6))
    pm.Bernoulli("response", p=p_yes, observed=rating)


def prepare_observed(rows):
    """Rows carry `number_set` ("16,8", in presented order), `target` and `rating`."""
    sets = [tuple(int(x) for x in str(r["number_set"]).split(",")) for r in rows]
    unique = list(dict.fromkeys(sets))
    index = {s: i for i, s in enumerate(unique)}
    set_log_lik = np.stack([EXAMPLE_LOG_LIK[:, np.array(s) - 1].sum(axis=1) for s in unique])
    out = {}
    for name, part in [("rule", slice(0, N_RULES)), ("interval", slice(N_RULES, None))]:
        log_lik = set_log_lik[:, part]
        log_evidence = logsumexp(log_lik, axis=1)
        out[f"{name}_log_evidence"] = log_evidence
        out[f"{name}_in_concept"] = np.exp(log_lik - log_evidence[:, None]) @ MEMBERSHIP[part]
    out["row_cell"] = np.array([index[s] * 100 + int(r["target"]) - 1 for s, r in zip(sets, rows)], dtype="int64")
    out["rating"] = np.array([int(r["rating"]) for r in rows], dtype="int64")
    return out
EOF

content.text:
I wrote the candidate, a decision-threshold model named `soft_confidence_criterion_decision`, and the admission check prints `OK`. Its short test fit scored about the same as the current best model (log-likelihood −906.1 against −905.8), so it probably won't beat it. The check doesn't test novelty, and with one chain it couldn't confirm convergence (R-hat).

**Hypothesis:** People infer the concept the same way as the simplest current model: Bayesian concept learning over equal-prior arithmetic and digit rules plus size-weighted intervals. What changes is the answer step. Instead of saying "yes" with the probability that the concept contains the target, they say "yes" when their confidence passes a personal criterion. Answers are graded around that point rather than all-or-none.

**Model:** three free parameters:
- **Rule prior share:** how much prior belief goes to the rules as a group versus the intervals.
- **Criterion:** how sure someone must be before saying "yes".
- **Gain:** how sharply answers change as confidence moves past the criterion.

With a gain below 1, near-certain beliefs turn into less certain answers. That covers stray "no" answers to clear members without adding a separate guessing rate.

- **Speed:** everything that doesn't depend on the parameters is computed once per example set before sampling, so the 200-iteration test fit took about a second. The full 7,000-iteration fit should be well inside the 30-minute limit.
- **Fit:** this ties the guessing-lapse model rather than beating it. Changes to how people answer, as opposed to how they infer the concept, look worn out on this data. I saved that in the agent notes so later rounds don't propose more of them.

The files are in `iter_2/candidate_2/`:
- `hypothesis.md`
- `model_name.txt`
- `candidate.py`
